## The pool

The Arkiv bounty pool for ETHRome 2026 is EUR 2,500. It is separate from the sponsorship, and
the Arkiv team manages and distributes it directly.

## How to qualify

To qualify you need BOTH, and both are pass/fail:

1. at least one of the three missions completed, and
2. all five requirements met.

Neither is scored. You are either in or you are not. Everything that IS scored happens after
that, on the single ranking below.

## Prizes

Mission 01 [Decommission] EUR 500, to the best qualifying entry that completed it.
Mission 02 [Built to expire] EUR 500, to the best qualifying entry that completed it.
Mission 03 [Live wire] EUR 500, to the best qualifying entry that completed it.
[Best Use of Arkiv] EUR 1,000, to the strongest qualifying project overall. Every qualifying
project competes for it automatically.

NOTE: Doing 3/3 does not pay three times, it puts you in three prize lines but you can only
win once.

## One prize per team, and what happens to the other one

One prize per team. If the team that would take a mission's EUR 500 has already won Best Use of
Arkiv, that EUR 500 passes to the next team that completed the same mission. If no other team
completed it, it is not paid.

## The three missions

Tick at least one mission: 1/3, 2/3 or 3/3.

MISSION 01 ⇒ DECOMMISSION

Done when: your app answers, from Arkiv, a question it answers today through a subgraph, Ponder
or a Postgres pipeline, and its read path no longer calls the indexer.

The decision that decides it: what goes in attributes, which you can query, versus what goes in
the payload, which you cannot. Get it wrong and every query turns into a scan. Aim for a
compound filter, not single-attribute equality.

We check: we run your query and see the question answered, and you link the commit from before
the migration. You never have to prove a hosted service is switched off. If you did not arrive
with an indexer already running, pick another mission rather than inventing one to turn off.

MISSION 02 ⇒ BUILT TO EXPIRE

Done when: something in your app changes because data expired on its own, not because a job
deleted it (think of expiration as a feature, not as a nice 'add-on')

Two patterns: let an entity lapse and treat its absence as the signal, or extend it on activity,
which gives you a lease, a sliding expiry that nothing has to maintain.

We check: the same query before and after the boundary, with no delete call in between. Keep
lifetimes at seconds or a couple of minutes, because we cannot wait on Sunday morning. A
recording made on Saturday counts.

How to actually hit "seconds or a couple of minutes" on Tiramisu, which is not obvious:

An Arkiv expiry is counted in BLOCKS, not in seconds, and the SDK converts your duration at a
nominal 2 seconds per block. Tiramisu does not promise a wall-clock cadence — it produces blocks
with network work. Measurements on 2026-09-04 ranged from 3 blocks/minute while idle to 30
blocks/minute under load. The same `ExpirationTime.fromMinutes(2)` therefore ranged from about
twenty real minutes to about two.

So for anything you have to demonstrate live:

- use ExpirationTime.fromBlocks(n), not fromSeconds / fromMinutes / fromDays;
- read expiresAt back from the receipt and treat it as the truth, not your stopwatch;
- expect it to move. Network load changes the cadence, so the same code can expire much sooner
  or later than it did when you rehearsed it.

We will print the current block cadence on this page during the event.

MISSION 03 ⇒ LIVE WIRE

Done when: your app updates from a subscription rather than from a refresh loop of your own.

Know this before you pick it: the SDK's subscribe helper only opens a real socket if your client
uses a websocket transport. With an HTTP transport it quietly polls once a second and the code
looks identical. Passing a start block to replay history forces polling too, so the backfill you
reach for after a dropped connection is the very thing that turns your subscription back into a
loop. Working that out is the mission; put what you find in your friction.md.

We check: the line where you build the client, showing a websocket transport, and your live
subscription with no start block. A two-wallet demo on its own cannot tell a socket from a poll,
so we need both: the code and the demo (one of you writes, the other's screen updates without a
refresh), plus a few lines on what happened when you dropped the connection.

Needs a live websocket endpoint. If one is not available during the event we will say so at the
opening and this mission is off; the other two and the EUR 1,000 are unaffected.

## The five requirements

PENDING SANTIAGO'S APPROVAL — these five are not in the printed manual and are not final until
he signs them off. They are published here in draft so nobody builds against a blank page. If
they change before the opening on Friday 11 September 16:00 CEST, the change is listed in the
changelog at the bottom of this page. After the opening they do not change at all.

R1. /arkiv/schema.md — your data model. At least two entity types; typed attributes with at
least one numeric; at least two queries written with real operators, at least one of them
combining two; the Entity Expiration you chose per type and why that one; and what you
deliberately left off Arkiv. This is the one the Friday workshop sends you home with a draft of.
Due Sunday 10:30 CEST.

R2. /arkiv/submission.md in a public repo. It ticks the mission or missions you completed and
links to everything else, including R1. It is the only door: we do not ask anyone to explain
their project. Due Sunday 10:30 CEST.

R3. The mission you completed IS your query evidence. There is no second demo to build. We run
the query ourselves against the network, or your arkiv/query.test.ts against a fixture if the
network is not cooperating. A JSON blob of rows pasted by hand does not count. Due Sunday
10:30 CEST.

R4. /arkiv/friction.md — at least three dated bullets, each one saying what you expected, what
happened, and how to reproduce it. There is a section per surface: SDK, docs, access keys and
faucet, block explorer, network, anything else. The proof is the commit timestamp. DUE
SATURDAY 20:00 CEST — this one cannot be done on Sunday morning.

R5. A ten-minute conversation with us, and five to eight sentences in your README on what
breaks if this were Postgres instead. We keep the log of the conversation, so there is no
sign-off to collect and nothing for you to chase. DUE SATURDAY 20:00 CEST for the
conversation; the README paragraph is due Sunday 10:30 CEST with the rest.

Our goal here is feedback, and use cases for Arkiv. We are an early product and we came to Rome
to find our own broken edges: docs, faucet, API keys, the SDK, Arkiv features, the explorer.
Forty people using all of it at once over one weekend is the best test we can get. That is why
every entry files a friction report, why its quality is a fifth of the score, and why the
ten-minute conversation is a requirement rather than a nice-to-have.

## Scores

Scores, for the entries that qualified:

Query depth 30 · evidence and reproducibility 20 · Arkiv fit and trade-offs 20 · friction
quality 20 · craft 10.

Craft means clarity, reliability and completeness, not visual polish. This single ranking
decides Best Use of Arkiv and, within each mission, who takes its EUR 500.

## Not eligible

Not eligible:

- the SDK installed but never queried;
- a Postgres app with our logo on it;
- a mission ticked without the check that mission asks for;
- keys, secrets or personal data written to Arkiv. Entities are public and verifiable by
  design. Store a hash or a commitment instead.

## How and when to submit

Submit through the event's official submission process, with a public repo. Everything we score
has to be in the repo by judging on Sunday 10:30 CEST. Two things close earlier and cannot be
done on Sunday morning: your friction report and the ten-minute conversation with us, both by
SATURDAY 20:00 CEST. Tell us your repo URL when we talk on Saturday.

## How winners get paid

Prizes are paid directly by Golem Factory GmbH (the Arkiv team) as a grant for delivered
open-source work. ETHRome / WER handle no part of it.

- Winners are announced at the closing ceremony on Sunday 13 September, 15:00.
- KYC opens the next business day and is run by our team, through a secure form we send to
  winners directly. We will never ask for identity documents over Discord, email or a shared
  sheet.
- One payee per winning team completes KYC; the rest of the team signs a one-page authorisation
  naming that payee. We are not going to ask five people for passports over a EUR 500 prize.
- Funds are sent within 10 business days of a complete KYC pack.
- One prize per team. Taxes are the winner's own responsibility.

The exact payment rail — network and currency — is with our finance and legal team. The final
wording lands on this page as soon as we have it.

## Where to find us

Santiago Trujillo Zuluaga, Sr. Developer Relations — data modelling, the SDK, and the bounty
gate. Telegram @SantiagoDevRel.
Shantelle Awomoyi, Head of Ecosystem — the opening keynote, on-site support, and the prize and
KYC process.

We walk the floor rather than sit at the table, especially on Saturday. If we are not at our
spot, ask an organiser to ping us. We are with teams all Saturday until 20:00 CEST.

## This page freezes

This page is the bounty. It freezes at the opening on Friday 11 September, 16:00 CEST. After
that, nothing here changes: anything we need to clarify goes in the changelog at the bottom,
